overview: The Medford School Committee swore in elementary class officers, presented student achievement awards, and reviewed updates on standardized testing, grants, public health protocols for tuberculosis, and the Every Student Succeeds Act. The committee also took positions on state legislative resolutions and a charter school ballot question.

items.title: Columbus Elementary School Class Officers Inauguration
items.summary: The committee celebrated the Fourth Grade Columbus Elementary School election results and administered the oath of office to newly elected class officers.

items.title: Presentation of MASS Student Achievement Awards
items.summary: Superintendent Roy Belson presented the Massachusetts Association of School Superintendents Student Achievement Award to Medford High School senior Zachary Rice and recognized vocational student Valerie Sajud.

items.title: Approval of Minutes, Bills, and Payrolls
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from September 26, 2016, along with routine bills, fund transfers, and payrolls.

items.title: Curriculum Subcommittee Report on 2016 Test Results
items.summary: Paulette Van der Kloot presented the Curriculum Subcommittee report reviewing 2016 PARCC and MCAS test performance, subgroup data, and transition plans for state assessments.

items.title: CPAC Presentation on High-Needs Students
items.summary: CPAC Co-Chair Melanie Perkins McLaughlin presented recommendations regarding high-needs students and district goals, leading the committee to approve scheduling a Committee of the Whole meeting within two months.

items.title: Report on Elementary School Grants
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Diane Caldwell reported on multiple local and state grants awarded to elementary school teachers for math, reading, cultural, and environmental initiatives.

items.title: Report on Tuberculosis Response and Action Steps
items.summary: Health Services Supervisor Toni Wray and Superintendent Roy Belson outlined contact tracing and scheduled testing protocols following a diagnosed tuberculosis case at the high school.

items.title: Report on DESE Planning for ESSA Accountability System
items.summary: Superintendent Roy Belson presented an overview of the federal transition from No Child Left Behind to the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA) and its potential funding and assessment impacts.

items.title: Report on Snow Day and School Cancellation Protocols
items.summary: Superintendent Roy Belson explained the inter-agency coordination, safety considerations, and municipal factors that determine weather-related school closures.

items.title: MASC Resolutions and Ballot Question Position
items.summary: The committee endorsed four statewide MASC legislative resolutions and passed a local resolution opposing Question 2 on charter school expansion.

items.title: Proclamation for Lights On After School Day
items.summary: Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke proclaimed October 22, 2016, as Lights On After School Day in Medford.

items.title: Condolences and Operational Updates
items.summary: The committee expressed condolences for several deceased community members and discussed routine updates on the School Brains software rollout, MBTA student passes, crossing guards, and upcoming community events.
